title: Sanity routing state reconciliation and variant-drift remediation
creator: Riley Nakamura
description: Summary: After a capacity-related degradation on 2026-03-08, smart-routing began selecting incompatible model variants for a subset of traffic. That triggered cascading cross-region reroutes and sustained request amplification for ~27 minutes. This ticket tracks the follow-up work: root-cause fixes, short-term mitigations, telemetry gaps closed, tests to prevent regressions, and operational runbook updates.
timeline: 2026-03-08: 03:15 UTC incident detected (elevated error rates and rising tail latency). 03:20 UTC mitigations: traffic pinning to failover region. 03:45 UTC service engineers confirmed variant incompatibility as the primary cause (KV cache handshake mismatch + policy precedence inversion). 04:10 UTC traffic normalized after manual policy freeze. 2026-03-10: Incident review and RCA completed. 2026-03-13: Engineering follow-ups kicked off and prioritized.
investigation_notes: Root causes identified: 1) Policy propagation ordering could interleave (edge case) causing policy precedence inversion when simultaneous policy updates and autoscaling events occur. 2) Variant compatibility check relied on eventual KV tag propagation and did not enforce immediate handshake validation. 3) TTLs on route state allowed stale precedence to persist for several minutes causing repeated fallback attempts. 4) Telemetry lacked a single signal correlating outgoing variant selection and incoming model rejection errors, which made triage slower.
decisions: 1) Implement synchronous variant-compatibility handshake for route transitions (short-circuit on mismatch). 2) Introduce a per-route TTL lockdown during policy changes (write lock) for 30s to avoid interleaving updates. 3) Add a circuit breaker that prevents immediate cross-region retries for the same session after N mismatches (configurable N=3). 4) Expand router telemetry to emit a single correlation id across policy decisions and model responses.

progress_updates: 2026-03-10: RCA session completed; validated that policy ordering race is plausible under burst autoscaling. Action items assigned.
2026-03-11: Prototype compatibility handshake implemented in feature branch; unit tests added. Observed ~1.2ms median added latency in microbenchmarks, acceptable under SLO.

2026-03-12: Policy write-lock TTL design reviewed by infra leads; agreed to default 30s with runtime override. Open concern: long lock on very noisy control planes; mitigation: adaptive TTL based on change frequency.
2026-03-13: Circuit breaker design reviewed; decided to keep session-scoped counters and a regional failover cap. Began instrumentation work for correlation id.
2026-03-13: QA test harness skeleton merged to qa/simulate/variant-drift branch; needs wider test vectors from product team.
risks_and_open_questions: 1) Compatibility handshake introduces extra round-trip—how does this affect tight latency SLOs for premium customers? 2) Adaptive TTL heuristic needs tuning to avoid unnecessary lock churn. 3) Circuit breaker thresholds must be conservative to avoid masking genuine capacity failovers.
runbook_changes: Add new detection rule: spike in 'variant_rejection' error events correlated with repeated route reassignment within 60s -> trigger automated policy-freeze and paged alert. Include manual mitigation steps to apply emergency variant pinning and rollback recent policy changes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for handshake and policy lock; integration tests in staging that simulate delayed KV propagation; chaos test that toggles autoscaling while publishing policy updates; regression test added to nightly suite.
deliverables_and_milestones: M1 (2026-03-18): Compatibility handshake merged to canary. M2 (2026-03-20): Policy write-lock deployed to staging + telemetry dashboards. M3 (2026-03-24): Circuit breaker + runbook updates deployed to production with monitoring for 72h.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No reroute echo observed in staging when simulating KV propagation delays for 60 minutes. 2) Telemetry shows correlation id for >99% of variant selection flows. 3) Circuit breaker prevents >95% of repeated cross-region retries after mismatch. 4) Runbook validated by SRE drill.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviewers on latency impact of handshake and edge cases for the TTL lockdown. Product PM should validate acceptable customer experience tradeoffs for short route locks. Security: double-check no sensitive material is emitted in the new correlation logs.
